statements.text: Pennsylvanians are concerned about the future, and we have a responsibility to offer them safety, security, and peace of mind. I support creating an AI regulatory framework that is human-focused. We need to support innovation and competition, not stifle it, with an approach that is pro-innovation with reasonable guardrails to protect people and their jobs.
I oppose those tax breaks and believe we can’t afford to let homeowners pay higher electric and water bills because of these data centers.
AI should enhance our work, not replace our work. I support creating a regulatory framework that places humans at the center of progress.

We definitely want to be leaders in the world, but we need to make sure that AI works for us and not that we work for AI. A lot of people are worried about losing their jobs, their livelihoods. We need to make sure that doesn’t happen. [...] We just need to make sure that we have regulations so that AI, which sounds like it’s going to be one of the biggest things that’s ever happened on this earth, we need to make sure that humans are in charge of it.
statements.venue: PA-10 debate with Scott Perry (as quoted by City & State PA)

statements.text: The most important thing here is to make sure that state and local authorities have the ability to say no without being punished.
statements.venue: PA-10 debate with Scott Perry (as quoted by Heartland Signal)
